nodes.title: Prompt Pixaroma (1. your prompt with the words)

promptState.text: A real photograph of a tall black chalkboard menu in a small neighbourhood bakery, front-on, the board filling almost the whole picture, centred, with a narrow strip of brick wall above it and at both sides. The board has a plain oak frame and stands against a whitewashed brick wall. Everything on the board is hand-lettered in chalk by a skilled sign painter. At the top, centred, is a small chalk line drawing of a round bunny head with two long upright ears, two dot eyes, a small nose and a little smile. Below it, with a clear gap of bare board between them, is the title "PIXA'S BAKERY" in big white chalk serif capitals. Under the title, "FRESH EVERY MORNING" runs in small orange chalk capitals between two thin white chalk lines. Below that are six evenly spaced rows, each with the name in white chalk capitals at the left, the price in orange chalk at the right, and one smaller line of neat white chalk handwriting under the name. Row 1: "CARROT CAKE" at the left, "$4.50" at the right, and under it "with cream cheese frosting". Row 2: "CINNAMON ROLL" at the left, "$3.25" at the right, and under it "warm from the oven". Row 3: "BLUEBERRY MUFFIN" at the left, "$2.75" at the right, and under it "with a crisp sugar top". Row 4: "BUTTER CROISSANT" at the left, "$2.50" at the right, and under it "flaky and golden". Row 5: "APPLE PIE SLICE" at the left, "$3.75" at the right, and under it "served with warm custard". Row 6: "HOT COCOA" at the left, "$3.00" at the right, and under it "topped with tiny marshmallows". At the very bottom of the board, centred, is one line of small white chalk script: "Baked with love by a very small bunny". The bottom of the frame stands on a worn oak counter that runs along the bottom of the picture. On the counter, lower than the writing on the board, stand a small white plate of three glazed cinnamon rolls at the left and a short glass jar of wooden spoons at the right, both whole. Clear morning daylight from a window at camera-left falls evenly across the board, with a soft shadow from the frame on the wall at the right. The palette is matte black, chalk white and honey oak, with the orange chalk as the one accent. Shot straight on from the middle height of the board with a 50mm lens at f/8, the board square to the camera and every word sharp. True-to-life colour, the dusty grain of real chalk strokes with faint grey smudges on the board, a little fine film grain.

{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Put exact words on a picture: a menu, a sign, a label, a cover. The nodes are the same as in workflow 1. What changes is the prompt: it lists every word and says where it goes. The demo menu has more than 50 words and prices.

 Steps

  1. Write your words in Prompt Pixaroma, or change the ones in the demo.
  2. Pick a size on Sizes Pixaroma. Many small words need a big size.
  3. Leave the seed on F to repeat a picture, or switch it to R for a new one each Run.
  4. Press Run, then zoom in and read every word.

 Writing the words

  • Put each word you want in double quotes, once: the title "PIXA'S BAKERY".
  • Say how it looks and where it goes: in big white chalk serif capitals at the top.
  • For a list, go from top to bottom: Row 1: "HOT COCOA" at the left, "$3.00" at the right.
  • Describe a small drawing too: two dot eyes, a small nose and a little smile. Without that, the bunny lost its face on one seed.
  • Keep things away from the words: a low plate on the counter stayed clear, but baking paper rose up and covered part of a word.

 Good to know

  • Read every word at full size. Big capitals hold up best. Small handwriting is where it slips: vanilla came out as vanila on three of four seeds, and crunchy as cruschy.
  • A word keeps slipping? Swap it for an easier one. We changed crunchy to crisp and a scoop of vanilla to warm custard. After that, all four seeds had every word right.
  • This many words need a big size. At 8 megapixels all four seeds of the demo had every word right. At 2 megapixels two seeds had a slip (golden became gelden, and $2.50 became $2.55). At 1 megapixel the big capitals and prices stayed right, but the small handwriting came apart on all four.
  • Full HD is 1920 x 1088 here: type 1080 and the model gives you 1072. HD (1280 x 720), 2K and 4K come out exact.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Save to your own folder Nodes look different from the video

{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (MiniMax H3 fl2va) - MiniMax H3, the video model. The LoRA in the next node turns it into P-H3 Image, a picture model. If you did Episode 41 you may already have this file.
  • LoRA Loader Pixaroma (P-H3 Image) - The P-H3 Image LoRA from Pruna. Keep it on at strength 1: without it H3 is a video model and the picture falls apart.
  • Load CLIP (P-H3 Image text encoder) - Reads your prompt and turns the words into something the model understands. The type must be minimax.
  • Load VAE (P-H3 Image VAE) - Turns the finished render into the picture. It is made for P-H3 Image, a different file from the H3 video VAE.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Prompt Pixaroma (1. your prompt with the words) - The prompt box. Every word on the board is in double quotes, in the order you read it from top to bottom. Change the words and keep the shape of the prompt.
  • Sizes Pixaroma (2. picture size) - The picture size. Click a size; the Portrait / Landscape switch turns it on its side. From top to bottom: 1, 2, 4 and 8 megapixels, three shapes each. The labels mark 1K, HD, Full HD, 2K and 4K. Many small words need a big size.
  • Seed Pixaroma (3. fixed or random) - The seed. F (fixed) gives the same picture every Run, R (random) a new one each Run. The demo uses seed 2.

 Working in the background

Teal. They run by themselves. The line next to each one says if there is anything worth changing.

  • MiniMaxH3SigmaShift (1 / 1 for pictures) - The noise schedule. P-H3 Image needs 1 and 1. Leave it as it is.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • PH3 Image Conditioning (prompt + size) - Joins the prompt and the size, and makes the empty canvas the picture is painted on.
  • Basic Guider (no CFG) - Hands the model and the prompt to the sampler. P-H3 Image needs no CFG and no negative prompt.
  • KSampler Select (sampler) - The sampler. euler is the one in Pruna's own workflow. ComfyUI's template uses er_sde: the same speed, but it broke small words on a label in our tests.
  • Manual Sigmas (the 8 steps) - The 8 steps the model was trained on. More steps do not help, so leave these numbers as they are.
  • Random Noise - The starting noise, from the seed.
  • Sampler Custom Advanced (the render) - The render itself: 8 steps. The normal KSampler cannot take this hand-made step list, so this node does the job.
  • VAE Decode (latent to picture) - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Image Pixaroma (saves the picture) - Saves each picture as PNG into ComfyUI/output/P-H3 Image Words and shows it on the node.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Nodes Info","icon":"node-v5","color":"#3d7cc9"}}

{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: a smaller picture is much faster.

SizeTime
1 megapixelabout 5 s
2 megapixelsabout 6 s
4 megapixelsabout 10 s
8 megapixels (the demo is 8)about 20 s

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models (about 20 GB for H3, and 10 GB for the LoRA, the text encoder and the VAE), so it takes longer. After that they stay in memory, if your PC has enough of it. Two testers with 16 GB cards: with 64 GB of RAM the next Runs were close to the times above; with 32 GB the models loaded from disk again on every Run, and each Run took about 4 times as long.

 On a smaller card

Start with a 1 or 2 megapixel size, the first six on Sizes Pixaroma. They look good too.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
